behavior: Per-run plan and state paths use domain-validated IDs. Root and child guidance and compaction reference the current run.
Native control-plane readers prefer per-session state and validate witnessed session/run/plan identity; a foreign present session file cannot fall back to global.
All prompt context/index/memory and brief writes are session-scoped; index contains the actual sessionId.

Legacy global materials are automatically reused only with verifiable matching identity. Explicit foreign session identity is rejected even when run IDs match. Unidentified old files remain explicitly readable historical artifacts.
Project sources, shared research materials and prior deliverables are retained. No concurrency prohibition, schema migration, manual approval or whole-package gate introduced.

Ordinary dispatch legacy projections must carry the actual platform run.id; missing run IDs are unattributed. Test fixtures were explicitly bound to start/dispatch returned IDs rather than weakening this requirement.
regressions: Real plugin plan calls overlap on a two-writer barrier in the same workspace; plan/state/brief/context remain distinct.
Both session context dispatches execute concurrently and preserve their own context/memory/index.
Same-session follow-up/repair restores revision and task state.
Child delegation and compaction inherit the active parent run, excluding a newer historical row.
Missing own materials, unidentified global legacy and explicitly foreign global identity are not injected.
Identity-bound legacy state/material remains compatible; foreign session and stale native run are rejected.
